title: The fog that turned London black for 5 days 🌫️
subject: fog
description:
Could a city vanish in smog like this today? 👇

In December 1952, the Great Smog covered London for 5 days. Coal smoke trapped under still, cold air turned the fog yellow-black, people couldn't see their own feet, and buses were guided by conductors with flashlights. About 4,000 deaths were counted at the time; later estimates reach 12,000. It led to the Clean Air Act of 1956.

Sources: Met Office ("The Great Smog of 1952"), London Museum ("Five days of pollution which killed 12,000"), History.com

scenes.text: People couldn't see their own feet. Bus conductors walked ahead of buses with flashlights.
Cinemas closed because nobody could see the screen.
It was December 1952. Freezing Londoners burned huge amounts of coal, and still air trapped the smoke over the city.
But here's the strange part. It wasn't just fog. It was soot, mixed with sulfuric acid.
About 4,000 people died in days, and later estimates reach 12,000. Four years later, Britain passed the Clean Air Act.
